stem: Seven people M, N, O, P, Q, R and S are sitting in a row. M is at the leftmost end. O is immediately left of N, and N is third from the right. R is immediately left of S. P is not adjacent to M. Q is not at either end, and Q is to the right of N. Who is third from the left?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Ignoring that P is not adjacent to M and freely placing P at position 2 forces the remaining arrangement to put P at position 3.
Reading 'Q is to the right of N' as 'Q is to the left of N' places Q in position 3 in the resulting arrangement.
Confusing 'R immediately left of S' with 'R at third from left' directly places R at position 3 without working through the full chain.

M=1, N=5 (third from right in a 7-person row), O=4 (immediately left of N). R immediately left of S: the RS pair fits positions 2-3 or 3-4, but O=4 blocks position 4 for S, so R=2, S=3. Q right of N and not at end: Q=6. P fills position 7. Verify P not adjacent to M: |7-1|=6, ok. Final: M-R-S-O-N-Q-P. Third from left = S.

explanation: M=1, O=4, N=5 (third from right). RS pair: O=4 blocks S from being at 4, so R=2, S=3. Q must be right of N(5) and not at end 7, so Q=6. P=7. Arrangement: M-R-S-O-N-Q-P. Third from left = position 3 = S.

explanation_sections.punchline: O=4 blocks the RS pair from occupying positions 3-4, forcing R=2 and S=3 which is the third from left.
explanation_sections.approach: Apply most-certain first: N=5 (third from right of 7), O=4 (immediately left of N). RS pair must sit in adjacent free seats: options are (2,3), (3,4) - blocked by O at 4, or (6,7) - but Q needs a non-end seat right of N. So R=2, S=3. Q=6, P=7. Verify P(7) not adjacent to M(1): distance 6, ok.
explanation_sections.lesson: When an adjacency pair has multiple candidate positions, use occupied-seat elimination to find the one valid placement.
explanation_sections.timing: About 85 s. Trap: placing RS at positions 6-7 and forgetting Q needs a non-end seat right of N.
